title: Your 90-Day Transition Action Plan
summary: Complete the course by combining your career direction, verified requirements, gaps, evidence, portfolio, deadlines, applications, support network, and backup routes into a practical 90-day action plan.
objectives: Identify verified requirements, deadlines, dependencies, and support contacts.
Define progress checks without creating a readiness or placement score.

vocab.def: A short-term transition plan organizing actions across approximately the next three months.
A planned moment for reviewing progress, new information, blockers, and next actions.
A condition preventing a planned next step from moving forward.
An intentional update to a plan based on new facts or circumstances.

sections.heading: Bring the course together
sections.body: Use what you learned about professionalism, communication, teamwork, safety, problem solving, digital literacy, accessibility, ethics, career planning, presentation, evidence, portfolio use, and financial readiness.

sections.heading: Plan the next 30, 60, and 90 days
sections.body: Organize actions into manageable periods while accounting for dependencies and external decisions.

sections.heading: Track facts, not imagined outcomes
sections.body: Record what is completed, submitted, scheduled, verified, accepted, declined, or pending without inventing readiness, placement, credential, or employment claims.

sections.heading: A transition plan is meant to change
sections.body: Revise the plan when new requirements, opportunities, deadlines, feedback, or circumstances appear.

practice.prompt: An apprenticeship has not opened applications yet. What should the plan show?
practice.answer: The verified current status, when to check again, useful preparation steps, and an alternate route if appropriate.

practice.prompt: A learner completes every 30-day action. Does that automatically make them career-ready?
practice.answer: No. Career readiness, competency, credentials, eligibility, and employment remain separate governed facts.

quiz.question: What is the strongest purpose of a 90-day transition action plan?
options: Turn verified next steps into specific actions that can be reviewed and revised
quiz.answer: Turn verified next steps into specific actions that can be reviewed and revised

lab.objective: Create a 90-day plan containing career direction, verified requirements, gaps, 30/60/90-day actions, deadlines, dependencies, support contacts, opportunity steps, backup route, and checkpoints.

reflectionPrompt: What is the single most important action you can take next to move from career preparation into a real verified next step?
